headline: Responsibility is accepting ownership of your choices and their consequences—the price of freedom and power
universal_truth: Power and responsibility are inseparable; you can't have one without accepting the other
fun_facts: The word 'responsibility' literally means 'ability to respond'
Research shows taking responsibility increases sense of control and reduces anxiety
Children as young as three show desire for credit—and avoidance of blame
discussion_questions: What are you responsible for that you didn't choose?
When is it hardest to take responsibility?
How does avoiding responsibility affect your sense of power?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Blame is tempting. It shifts weight off your shoulders. But every time you blame circumstances, other people, or bad luck, you give away power. Responsibility is heavy—but it comes with control. Own your outcomes, and you can change them.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Taking responsibility feels bad in the moment—admitting fault, accepting consequences. Avoiding responsibility feels better immediately. So why is responsibility valuable?

options.text: Responsibility comes with power—if you caused it, you can change it; if you blame others, you're helpless until they change
options.response: Yes. Blaming is psychologically comfortable but practically powerless. Responsibility is uncomfortable but empowering. You can only improve what you own.
There's moral value, but the practical value is even more compelling...

q1.title: Responsibility and Control
q1.script: If you're responsible, you have power to change things. If circumstances are responsible, you're helpless. Even when something isn't your fault, asking 'what can I do about it?' is more useful than assigning blame.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Responsibility and Control"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Radical Ownership
q2.script: Extreme performers often take extreme responsibility. Athletes blame themselves for team losses. Leaders take responsibility for team failures. This isn't self-punishment—it's self-empowerment. What you own, you can improve.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Responsibility vs Guilt
q3.script: Responsibility isn't the same as guilt. You can accept responsibility without endless self-flagellation. 'I caused this, so I can fix it' is different from 'I caused this, so I'm terrible.' Responsibility is forward-looking; guilt is backward.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Power and responsibility are inseparable. You can't have control without accepting ownership. The freedom to change your life requires the weight of owning your outcomes.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 195. Tomorrow, we'll explore what fair really means—justice. Until then, identify something you've been blaming on circumstances and ask: what can I own about this?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Ownership Shift - Blame to Power
growTrack.activity: Identify something you've blamed on external factors—circumstances, other people, bad luck. Ask: What part of this am I responsible for? What could I do differently? Shifting from blame to ownership doesn't add guilt; it adds power.
